question: I append items to a Vec stored under one Persistent key. Why can later Soroban writes fail, and how should I store the collection?

golden.answer: Persistent storage changes durability, not entry layout. One key still maps to one serialized contract-data ledger entry, so a growing `Vec` or `Map` under that key grows one entry. The write fails when the serialized entry exceeds the target network's configured contract-data entry limit. Do not freeze a byte value or error string because the limit is network-controlled. Keep a one-entry collection explicitly bounded, or split an unbounded collection across distinct composite keys or bounded chunks. Fine-grained keys also avoid rewriting and contending on the whole collection.
keyFacts: A Vec or Map under one Persistent key remains one serialized contract-data ledger entry.
A growing collection can exceed the network-configured entry limit.
Splits an unbounded collection across keys or chunks.
avoid: Do NOT claim Persistent storage automatically shards a growing value across ledger entries.
Do NOT freeze a universal byte limit or exact failure string.
golden.notes: This case tests one Persistent value, not the separate Instance-storage DoS or nullifier-retention cases. Reward bounded one-entry layouts, composite per-item keys, or bounded chunks. The exact entry limit is network-controlled. Avoid item 2 targets a byte limit stated as universal or permanent. A dated or attributed current figure is not that claim.

corroboration.claim: A Vec or Map stored under one Persistent key remains one complete contract-data ledger entry.

evidence.note: The official data model defines one user key and one associated value per contract-data entry. Either can contain vectors or maps.
The Persistent API reads and writes one value through one supplied key.

corroboration.claim: A growing one-entry collection can exceed the network-controlled contract-data entry limit and should be bounded or split.

evidence.note: The official guide rejects unbounded vectors or maps under one key and recommends bounded or split layouts.
Core compares each contract-data entry size with the configured maximum and rejects an oversized entry.

corroboration.claim: As of 2026-10-01, the Mainnet contract-data entry limit is 65536 bytes (64 KiB), a validator-changeable network setting, and the official storage guide states the same figure with a dated check.
